text:
Sam: S3+Dynamo lock flapping again on gpu-cluster infra workspace. Applies stuck waiting on lock, GH Actions times out.

Maria: saw a CI timeout earlier, re-ran it and it succeeded. terraform error: "Error acquiring the state lock".

Vikram: same pattern this week. Long nodepool updates cause the runner to hold the lock longer than the TTL; GH Actions restarts leave a stale lease in DynamoDB.

Kevin: last year we added a short TTL (30s) on the lock table. Backend is S3 in us-west-2 + DDB. If an apply runs >10m the lease can expire and another runner takes over -> collision.

Sam: that matches the "lock flipper" symptoms: lease expires -> new process grabs lock -> old process resumes and hits Dynamo errors. We should either increase TTL or implement lease-renewal from CI.

Vikram: Terraform's S3+Dynamo locking doesn't auto-renew the TTL. The provider writes a single Dynamo item; the CI runner is responsible for heartbeats. If GH runner dies, heartbeat stops.

Maria: options we discussed:
- bump TTL to something safe (e.g. 20m)
- add a CI wrapper that periodically touches the lock (lock keeper)
- migrate locking to Terraform Cloud / Enterprise
- use an alternative locking backend (Consul sessions, etc)

Kevin: increasing TTL is the simplest but increases worst-case blocking time if a runner really crashes. For long-running ops we should prefer manual apply or out-of-band runs.

Vikram: practical proposal: keep plan in CI, gate apply behind a manual approval for nodepool/gpu infra changes. For automated applies we can prototype a small sidecar that polls and extends the Dynamo lease while the task process is alive.

Sam: we also have to recover a few half-applied resources (helm releases stuck, nodepool entries missing). Need a documented recovery recipe.

Maria: recovery steps I used before: 
1) Identify lock holder: query the DDB table for the LockID and holder info.
2) If holder is dead, delete the item: 
aws dynamodb delete-item --table-name tf-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"<id>"}}'
3) Run terraform init && terraform plan to inspect drift, then terraform apply when safe.

Warning: if an apply was mid-flight state may be inconsistent. Always run terraform plan and review diffs before applying.

Vikram: import example for nodepools created outside TF: 
```bash
terraform import module.gpu_nodepool.google_container_node_pool.gpu_pool projects/myproj/locations/us-west2-a/clusters/gpu-cluster/nodePools/gpu-pool
```
then run `terraform state list` and `terraform plan` to confirm.

Kevin: and when we refactor module addresses you can avoid recreate by `terraform state mv`: 
```bash
terraform state mv module.old_module.google_compute_instance.vm module.new_module.google_compute_instance.vm
```
That prevents destroy/create churn.

Sam: immediate playbook I'm going to run:
- freeze CI applies for gpu infra (add branch rule)
- perform human-led recovery from ops laptop with creds
- after recovery, adjust TTL and wrap apply jobs with lock keeper or manual approvals
- write docs with import/state-mv examples and exact commands used

Maria: I'll open a PR to add a "manual-apply" flag to the nodepool terraform pipeline and a pre-check that fails early if estimated plan time > 5m.

Vikram: I'll prototype a tiny lock-keeper tool (bash/python) that acquires the normal terraform lock and while the process PID is alive periodically calls `aws dynamodb update-item` to refresh TTL.

Kevin: confirm CI IAM includes dynamodb:UpdateItem for the lock table. Currently runners have PutItem/DeleteItem; we'll add UpdateItem if we go this route.

Maria: also propose adding an alert in Console for long-running plan/apply (>5m) so infra-oncall can intervene before TTL expiry.

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-032 - Terraform lock flapping for gpu-cluster. PagerDuty alerted to infra-oncall. https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-032

Sam: starting recovery at 1710668200 from ops laptop. Will paste commands & outputs here so we can capture them in the runbook.

Maria: please paste exact commands and outputs in this thread so I can add them to docs.

Vikram: post-recovery follow-ups: consider a longer-term migration to Terraform Cloud runs (handles long applies), or move cross-region backends to GCS / TF Cloud for customers with multi-region infra.

Kevin: joining the recovery run in 10m. Thanks team :thumbsup:
